nesnd_jp_mining_reason.zh: 征税和征兵曾是武士的本分，开矿、办厂却要仰仗商人。北方的矿藏给江户带来了新的财源，也带来了旧军府不熟悉的合作者。那些不佩刀的人正在积累财富，并开始要求政府保护他们的生意。
nesnd_jp_mining_reason.en: Collecting taxes and raising soldiers were once the duties of the warrior class. Mining and manufacturing require merchants as well. The mineral wealth of the north gives Edo new revenues, but also new partners: men without swords who are growing wealthy and expect the government to protect their businesses.

nesnd_jp_arsenals_reason.zh: 兵工厂和船坞把军费带进了城镇。承包商盼望长久的订单，军方则担心自己的装备受制于商人的价钱。工场越是兴旺，这场讨价还价就越难留在营门之外。
nesnd_jp_arsenals_reason.en: Arsenals and shipyards bring military spending into the towns. Contractors want dependable orders; officers resent having to bargain over the price of their equipment. As the workshops grow, these negotiations are becoming part of the business of government.

nesnd_jp_metal_cities_reason.zh: 城下町原本围着城郭与武士宅邸生长，如今来此谋生的人却越来越多。工人、学徒和小店主住进新街区，他们的孩子也要在这里读书。旧日替领主办事的城镇，正在长成有自己诉求的社会。
nesnd_jp_metal_cities_reason.en: The castle town grew around the lord’s fortress and the homes of his retainers. Now workers, apprentices and shopkeepers are settling in new streets, with children who need schooling. A town built to serve its lord is becoming a society with demands of its own.

nesnd_jp_cash_crops_reason.zh: 海港把远方的价钱带到了乡间。棉田、桑园和茶山有了新的买主，土地所有者与商人都想从中分得更多。农民日复一日的劳作，也开始受到这些遥远市场的支配。
nesnd_jp_cash_crops_reason.en: The ports bring the prices of distant markets into the countryside. Cotton, silk and tea have found new buyers, and both landowners and merchants want a larger share of the proceeds. The work of rural households is increasingly governed by decisions made far from their villages.

nesnd_jp_textiles_reason.zh: 收购生丝与棉花的商人开始把织工集中起来。熟悉的手艺进入了更大的工场，雇工按时领钱，也须服从工头的规矩。对于离开田地的人，这是新的生计；对于商人，则是把乡村生产握得更紧的办法。
nesnd_jp_textiles_reason.en: Merchants who once bought cotton and silk from scattered households are bringing weavers together in larger mills. Wage work offers a new livelihood to people leaving the land, though it also subjects familiar skills to the discipline of a foreman. For the merchants, it promises closer control over production.

nesnd_jp_consumer_goods_reason.zh: 食品、家具和日用器皿的生意，正在从少数富户扩展到更多家庭。经营这些工场的人开始关心普通人的收入：顾客若只能勉强糊口，再多的货物也只能堆在仓库里。
nesnd_jp_consumer_goods_reason.en: Food, furniture and household goods are finding customers beyond the wealthiest homes. Their manufacturers have acquired a reason to care about ordinary incomes. Families struggling to feed themselves cannot buy the goods waiting in their warehouses.

nesnd_jp_living_standards_reason.zh: 已经进入工场的人开始盘算房租、米价和孩子读书的钱。他们为城市带来了劳力与税收，也要求从繁荣中得到自己的份额。政府许诺的新生活，终究要落到这些日常开支上。
nesnd_jp_living_standards_reason.en: Families who have found work in the mills must still pay rent, buy food and find money for their children’s schooling. They have brought labour and tax revenue to the towns, and expect a share in their prosperity. The promise of a better life will be judged against these everyday expenses.

nesnd_jp_food_supply_reason.zh: 田间的收成、渔人的船和往来的粮商，维持着城里的生活。粮价一涨，官署里的争论很快便会传到街市。政府须让运粮的人愿意进城，也让城里的人买得起饭。
nesnd_jp_food_supply_reason.en: Harvests, fishing boats and grain merchants sustain life in the towns. A rise in food prices can carry a dispute from government offices into the streets. Food must reach the markets at prices townspeople can afford.

nesnd_jp_food_cities_reason.zh: 粮商带来了买卖，工匠和学徒也跟着留下。新街区需要学校，官府与书商需要纸张；许多过去由乡里宗族包办的事情，开始交到城镇的机构手中。
nesnd_jp_food_cities_reason.en: The grain trade brings customers, and craftsmen and apprentices settle near them. New neighbourhoods need schools; offices and booksellers need paper. Town institutions are taking on duties once left to village households and clans.

nesnd_jp_food_processing_reason.zh: 罐藏技术让粮食与鱼获能够保存得更久，也把收购、加工和远途运输变成了同一门生意。商人可以等待更好的价钱，工场里的雇工则希望生产不再随着收获季节一同停下。
nesnd_jp_food_processing_reason.en: Canning allows food and fish to be stored longer, bringing purchasing, processing and long-distance transport into a single trade. Merchants can wait for better prices, while workers hope the factories will offer employment beyond the harvest season.

nesnd_jp_court_reform_reason.zh: 旧臣们希望新政仍以君主的名义推行。商人和新学出身的官员则要求法令保障，免受临时征敛与地方势力的摆布。王朝能够把他们召集到一起，具体的权利却还要重新划分。
nesnd_jp_court_reform_reason.en: The old retainers want reform carried out in the monarch’s name. Merchants and officials trained in the new schools seek legal protection from arbitrary levies and local power. The crown can bring them together, but their respective rights remain to be settled.

nesnd_jp_nation_reason.zh: 争取独立时许下的承诺，正在成为政府必须回答的问题。军费由谁承担，关税由谁决定，地方权力又该划到哪里？出资的人和出力的人，都希望在新的国家里得到自己的位置。
nesnd_jp_nation_reason.en: The promises made in pursuit of independence now confront the government. Who will pay for defence, who will set the tariffs, and how much authority will remain in local hands? Those who contributed money and those who served expect a place in the new state.

nesnd_jp_development.1.d.zh:
各国使节如今直接同我们的政府交涉。过去借宗主之手维持的军政与海上往来，已经有了本国自己的制度。

当年支持独立的商人和地方人士并未因此退出国事。他们带着新的请愿来到政府面前，要求它兑现曾经许下的承诺。
nesnd_jp_development.1.d.en:
Foreign envoys now deal directly with our government. Defence and overseas affairs, once conducted through an overlord, rest on institutions of our own.

The merchants and local leaders who supported independence have not retired from public life. They have brought new petitions, expecting the government to honour its promises.

nesnd_jp_development.2.d_court.zh:
朝廷以新法确认了议政与任官的办法。旧臣仍在君主身边，地方官署却开始接纳另一批熟悉实务的人。

拥护王朝的改制派认为，这些让步足以使君主制延续下去。至于取得议政权的人们会不会满足，朝廷眼下还没有答案。
nesnd_jp_development.2.d_court.en:
The court has settled new arrangements for representation and public office. The monarch still has the company of old retainers, but provincial administration is admitting officials with a different education.

Reformers loyal to the crown believe these concessions will preserve the monarchy. Whether those who have gained a voice will be satisfied remains an open question.

nesnd_jp_development.2.d_military.zh:
主张集权的军官终于让自己的办法成为国策。征募、训练和军需被纳入更严密的组织，地方官员也须执行中央的命令。

他们把这一结果视为国家重新强盛的开端。军费的负担和军官的权力，却会长久留在民间的议论之中。
nesnd_jp_development.2.d_military.en:
Officers who argued for central authority have secured the policy they wanted. Recruitment, training and military supply are more closely organized, with local officials expected to carry out the government’s orders.

Its advocates see the beginning of renewed national strength. The cost of the army, and the power of its officers, will remain matters of public dispute.

nesnd_jp_development.2.d_representative.zh:
取得选举权的人开始用选票选择代表，报纸也能公开议论政府的行为。官员须面对新的任用办法，而议场内外的争论已经越出旧日少数家族的范围。

新学堂还在把更多人带进这个世界。下一代读书人将怎样运用这些权利，要由他们自己决定。
nesnd_jp_development.2.d_representative.en:
Those entitled to vote now choose their representatives, and newspapers can debate the conduct of government. Officials face new rules of appointment, while political argument has spread beyond the old ruling families.

Schools are bringing more people into this world. How the next generation will use these rights is theirs to decide.

nesnd_jp_foreign_reason.zh: 大陆朝廷的援军曾帮助丰臣平定日本，朝贡与海上贸易也由此同列岛的政治纠缠在一起。我们所争取的自主权，关系着宗主的收入、海防和对日本的控制；即使旧约解除，这些利益也不会随之消失。
nesnd_jp_foreign_reason.en: Aid from the mainland court helped the Toyotomi subdue Japan, binding tribute and maritime trade to the politics of the islands. Greater autonomy touches an overlord’s revenue, naval interests and influence in Japan. Those interests endure even when the old obligations are dissolved.

nesnd_jp_korea_reason.zh: 朝鲜南部的煤矿和港口支撑着跨海的商业。当地商人需要这些航路，地方士人却不愿把民政全交给海峡对岸的官员。乡里最常争论的，往往是下一笔税款归谁处置。
nesnd_jp_korea_reason.en: The mines and ports of southern Korea sustain trade across the strait. Local merchants depend on those routes, while provincial elites resist surrendering civil affairs to officials from across the sea. Arguments often come down to who will control the next levy.

nesnd_jp_foreign.1.d6.zh: [SCOPE.sCountry('jp_sender').GetNameNoFormatting]请求我们承认其政府主持日本的统一，并将本国领土交由对方统治。接受这份盟约，便是结束本国的单独存在。
nesnd_jp_foreign.1.d6.en: [SCOPE.sCountry('jp_sender').GetNameNoFormatting] asks us to recognize its government as the leader of Japanese unification and place our territory under its rule. Accepting would end our existence as a separate state.
